79344.e: Many houses, the arcades and the Minster in Bern are built of sandstone. Bernese sandstone is greenish grey.
79344.m: Bern's old town is built of sandstone.

79345.q: What happens if you rub your finger hard over old sandstone?
79345.e: Sandstone is not as solid as granite. If you rub it, single grains of sand often come loose.
79345.m: Grains of sand come off sandstone easily.

79346.q: Why did sculptors like working with sandstone?
79346.e: Sandstone is softer than many other stones. That is why it can easily be shaped with a chisel and hammer.

79347.q: Which famous red rock in Australia is made of sandstone?
79347.e: Uluru is a huge rock in the middle of Australia. It is made of sandstone and glows red at sunset.
79347.m: Uluru in Australia is made of sandstone.

79348.q: What wears sandstone down over time so that it crumbles?
79348.e: Rain, frost and wind gradually loosen grains from the sandstone. That is why old sandstone buildings often need repairing.
79348.m: Wind and rain make sandstone crumble.

79349.e: Depending on what is between the grains of sand, sandstone can be yellow, red, brown or grey. Red sandstone contains iron, for example.

79350.q: What did sandstone form from a very long time ago?
a: From sand on beaches, in rivers or deserts
79350.e: Sand settled in thick layers on beaches, in rivers or in deserts. Under pressure it slowly turned into solid stone.
79350.m: Sandstone formed from layers of sand.

79351.q: Which stone did marble form from?
79351.e: Marble forms when limestone deep inside the Earth is strongly heated and squeezed. This changes the stone.

79352.q: What is white marble especially famous for?
79352.e: White marble can be carved finely and has a lovely shine. That is why artists have made famous statues from it.
79352.m: Statues are made from white marble.

79353.q: Which country does the famous Carrara marble come from?
79353.e: Carrara is a town in Italy. White marble has been quarried there for over 2000 years.

79354.q: What stone is Michelangelo's famous statue “David” made of?
79354.e: Michelangelo carved “David” from a large block of white marble. The statue stands in Florence.

79355.q: Which famous building in India is built of white marble?
79355.e: The Taj Mahal in Agra is a tomb covered in white marble. The other buildings are made of red or pink sandstone.
79355.m: The Taj Mahal is made of white marble.

79356.q: Which little toy balls get their name from marble?
79356.e: In the past, these little balls were often made of marble. That is why they are called marbles.
79356.m: Marbles get their name from marble.

79357.e: Polished marble has a very smooth surface. It feels cool even on warm days.
79357.m: Polished marble is smooth and cool.

79358.q: How can you often recognise marble?
a: By its holes like in cheese
79358.e: Many kinds of marble have fine, coloured lines. These lines are called veins.

79359.q: What does a rock crystal look like?
79359.e: A rock crystal is colourless and see-through. It looks like clear glass or ice.
79359.m: A rock crystal is clear like glass.

79360.q: How many sides does a rock crystal have all the way round?
79360.e: A rock crystal is a column with six side faces. At the top it comes to a point.
79360.m: A rock crystal has six sides.

79361.q: What are people called in Switzerland who search the mountains for crystals?
79361.e: In Switzerland, crystal hunters are called Strahler. They climb around the Alps looking for crystals.
79361.m: In Switzerland, crystal hunters are called Strahler.

79362.q: Where in Switzerland can you find rock crystals?
a: In fields on the Central Plateau
79362.e: Rock crystals are found mainly in the Alps. The areas around the Grimsel and the Gotthard are especially well known.
79362.m: Rock crystals are found in the Swiss Alps.

79363.q: What did people long ago think a rock crystal was?
79363.e: In the past, many people believed rock crystal was ice that never melts. The word crystal comes from the Greek word for ice.
79363.m: People used to think rock crystal was everlasting ice.

79364.q: Which mineral family does rock crystal belong to?
79364.e: Rock crystal is a very pure, clear form of quartz. Quartz is one of the most common minerals.

79365.q: What shape is the top end of a rock crystal?
79365.e: A rock crystal grows as a six-sided column. Its top end comes together in a point.
79365.m: A rock crystal has a point.

79366.e: Rock crystals grow in cracks and hollows in the rock. Over a long time, quartz from the water builds up there.
79366.m: Rock crystals grow in hollows in the rock.

79367.q: How long do large rock crystals take to grow?
79367.e: Rock crystals grow very slowly. Large crystals need a great many years.

79368.e: The ruby is a red gemstone. Its name comes from the Latin word for red.

79369.e: The emerald is a bright green gemstone. It is one of the most valuable gemstones.

79370.q: What colour is a sapphire usually?
79370.e: Most sapphires are blue. But there are also sapphires in other colours.

79371.e: The amethyst is a purple gemstone. It is a form of quartz.

79372.e: Gemstones are rare, beautiful and hard. That is why they are very precious.
79372.m: Gemstones are rare and therefore valuable.

79373.q: What do people do to gemstones to make them sparkle?
79373.e: Gemstones are cut into shape. Their many smooth faces make them sparkle in the light.

79374.q: What are gemstones often used for?
79374.e: Gemstones are beautiful and rare. That is why they are often set in rings, necklaces and crowns.
79374.m: Gemstones are often used for jewellery.

79375.q: Which of a queen's treasures is often set with lots of gemstones?
79375.e: The crowns of queens and kings are often decorated with gemstones. They show power and wealth.
79375.m: Crowns are often set with gemstones.

79376.q: Which stone is the hardest in nature?
79376.e: Diamond is the hardest natural material. It can scratch almost every other substance.
79376.m: Diamond is the hardest stone in nature.

79377.q: What is a diamond made of?
79377.e: A diamond is made only of carbon. That is the same substance that coal is mostly made of.
79377.m: A diamond is made of carbon.

79378.q: What is the unit used for the weight of diamonds?
79378.e: The weight of diamonds and gemstones is measured in carats. One carat is 0.2 grams.

79379.q: Apart from jewellery, what are diamonds used for?
79379.e: Because diamonds are so hard, they are put into drills and saws. With them you can even cut hard stone.
79379.m: Diamonds help with cutting and drilling.

79380.q: What colour is a typical diamond?
79380.e: Most diamonds in jewellery are colourless and clear. But there are also rare coloured diamonds.

79381.q: What is a cut diamond in jewellery often called?
79381.e: A diamond with a special round cut is called a brilliant. This makes it sparkle especially strongly.
79381.m: A cut diamond is often called a brilliant.

79382.q: What can happen if you hit a diamond hard with a hammer?
79382.e: A diamond is very hard, but it is also brittle. A hard blow can therefore split or shatter it.
79382.m: A diamond is hard, but it can shatter if hit.

79383.e: Diamond is harder than glass. That is why you can scratch and cut glass with it.

79384.q: What do you use to pan for gold in the sand of a stream?
79384.e: You put sand and water into a flat pan and swirl it. The light bits are washed away and the heavy gold stays behind.
79384.m: You pan for gold with a gold pan.

79385.q: Why does gold stay at the bottom of the pan when panning?
79385.e: Gold is much heavier than sand and gravel. That is why it sinks to the bottom when you swirl the pan.
79385.m: Gold stays behind because it is heavy.

79386.q: What does gold that you find in a stream look like?
79386.e: In a stream you usually only find tiny flakes of gold. Big lumps of gold are very rare.
79386.m: In a stream you usually find tiny flakes of gold.

79387.q: Can you find gold in Swiss streams?
79387.e: In some streams, for example in the Napf area, the water carries tiny grains of gold. You hardly ever find big pieces.
79387.m: There are tiny grains of gold in some Swiss streams.

79388.q: What happens to gold if it lies in water for a long time?
79388.e: Gold does not rust and does not change in water. That is why it still shines even after a long time.

79389.q: What is a lump of gold found in nature called?
79389.e: A natural lump of gold is called a nugget. Bars and coins are made by people.
79389.m: A lump of gold from nature is called a nugget.

79390.q: What gets washed out of the pan when panning for gold?
79390.e: When you swirl the pan, the water washes out the lighter grains of sand and little stones. The heavy gold is left behind.
79390.m: When panning for gold, you wash the sand away.

79391.q: What is the time called when, from 1848, huge numbers of people moved to California to find gold?
79391.e: From 1848, thousands of people travelled to California to find gold. This time is called the Gold Rush.
79391.m: In the Gold Rush, lots of people searched for gold.

79392.e: Sand is made of small grains of rock. They have been worn off bigger stones by wind and water.
79392.m: Sand is made of tiny grains of rock.

79393.q: Which sand is better for building a sandcastle?
79393.e: Wet sand sticks together because the water holds the grains together. Dry sand trickles apart.
79393.m: You build sandcastles with wet sand.

79394.q: What is the largest hot desert on Earth, where there is lots of sand?
79394.e: The Sahara in Africa is the largest hot desert in the world. Part of it is covered with huge sand dunes.
79394.m: The Sahara is the largest hot desert.

79395.e: Sand is heated very strongly until it melts. This makes glass for windows and bottles.

79396.e: In an hourglass, sand trickles from the top to the bottom. When it has all run through, a certain amount of time has passed.

79397.q: What are the hills of sand called that the wind piles up in the desert?
79397.e: The wind blows the sand together into big hills. These hills are called dunes.
79397.m: Hills of sand in the desert are called dunes.

79398.q: What do you get if you mix sand, gravel, cement and water?
79398.e: Sand, gravel, cement and water together make concrete. When it dries it becomes rock hard, and houses and bridges are built with it.
79398.m: Concrete is made from sand, gravel, cement and water.

79399.q: What happens to water that you pour onto sand?
79399.e: There are lots of small gaps between the grains of sand. That is why water flows through sand quickly.
79399.m: Water soaks away quickly in sand.

79400.q: How does wet clay soil feel?
79400.e: Wet clay soil is soft and sticky and can be shaped. That is why it sticks to shoes and hands.
79400.m: Wet clay soil is sticky and soft.

79401.q: What happens to clay soil when it dries?
79401.e: When the water evaporates from the clay soil, it becomes firm and hard. It often cracks as it dries.

79402.q: What is made from clay that is fired in a kiln?
79402.e: Bricks are shaped from clay. They are fired in a hot kiln, which makes them very solid.
79402.m: Bricks are made from fired clay.

79403.q: Which bird builds its nest out of little lumps of mud?
79403.e: Swallows collect damp mud in their beaks. They use it to stick their nests onto house walls or inside barns.
79403.m: Swallows build their nests from mud.

79404.q: What can you shape out of clay?
79404.e: Clay is easy to shape. After firing, it becomes solid pots, bowls and jugs.
79404.m: You can shape pots out of clay.

79405.q: What have people in many countries built houses from, in the past and today?
79405.e: Clay soil can be found almost everywhere and it is cheap. That is why people in many countries build houses out of mud bricks.
79405.m: Many houses around the world are built of clay.

79406.q: Why does a puddle often stay on clay soil after rain?
a: Clay soaks up water straight away
79406.e: Clay has very fine grains that lie close together. That is why water only soaks into it slowly.

79407.q: What colour is clay soil often?
79407.e: Clay soil often contains iron. That is why it is usually brown, yellowish or reddish.
79407.m: Clay soil is usually brown or yellowish.

a: Remains of living things that turned to stone
A stone that has been painted
79408.e: A petrification shows remains or prints of living things from long ago. Over a very long time they turned to stone.
79408.m: A petrification is a living thing that turned to stone.

79409.q: What is another word for a living thing that has turned to stone?
79409.e: Remains of living things that have turned to stone are called fossils. A single piece is called a fossil.
79409.m: A living thing turned to stone is called a fossil.

79410.q: What does a fossil ammonite look like?
a: Like a snail shell with a spiral
79410.e: Ammonites were sea creatures with a spiral shell. Their fossils look like coiled snail shells.
79410.m: An ammonite looks like a spiral shell.

79411.q: How long does it take for a living thing to turn to stone?
79411.e: A fossil forms slowly over many thousands to millions of years. The living thing gets covered by layers of sand or mud.
79411.m: A fossil takes a very, very long time to form.

79412.q: What did dinosaurs leave behind that was found in the canton of Jura?
79412.e: In the canton of Jura there are thousands of fossil dinosaur footprints. They show where the animals walked long ago.
79412.m: There are fossil dinosaur tracks in the Jura.

79413.q: What are scientists who study fossils called?
79413.e: Palaeontologists study fossils. This is how they learn which animals and plants lived long ago. Archaeologists, on the other hand, study traces left by people.

79414.q: In which yellow resin stone do you sometimes find trapped insects?
79414.e: Amber is fossilised tree resin. Sometimes it contains trapped insects that lived millions of years ago.
79414.m: You sometimes find insects in amber.

79415.q: Why do people find fossil shells on Swiss mountains?
a: There used to be sea there
79415.e: A very long time ago there was a sea where Switzerland is today. Later the seabed was folded up into mountains.
79415.m: Where there are mountains today, there used to be sea.

79416.q: What does baking powder do in cake mixture?
a: It makes the mixture rock hard
79416.e: Baking powder forms lots of tiny gas bubbles in the mixture. These make the cake light and tall.
79416.m: Baking powder makes the mixture rise.

79417.q: Which gas is produced when baking powder works in dough?
79417.e: Baking powder releases the gas carbon dioxide. The gas bubbles puff up the dough.
79417.m: Baking powder makes the gas carbon dioxide.

79418.q: What is a sponge cake like if you forget the baking powder?
79418.e: Without baking powder, hardly any gas bubbles form in the mixture. The cake does not rise and stays flat and dense.
79418.m: Without baking powder, the cake stays flat.

79419.q: Where does baking powder work best?
79419.e: Baking powder needs moisture and, above all, heat. In a hot oven it makes the most gas.
79419.m: Baking powder works mainly in a hot oven.

79420.e: Baking powder is a fine white powder. That is why you can hardly see it in the mixture.
79420.m: Baking powder is a white powder.

79421.q: Which substance is the most important part of baking powder?
79421.e: Bicarbonate of soda forms gas bubbles in moist, warm dough. That is why it is the most important part of baking powder.
79421.m: Baking powder is mainly bicarbonate of soda.

79422.q: Why does a cake made with baking powder have lots of little holes inside?
79422.e: During baking, lots of gas bubbles form in the mixture. The cake sets and the holes stay.
79422.m: The holes in a cake come from gas bubbles.

79423.q: Which bake is usually made with baking powder?
79423.e: Cakes such as marble cake rise with baking powder. Pizza and bread are usually made with yeast.
79423.m: Marble cake is made with baking powder.

79424.e: Yeast is made of tiny living fungi. You can only see the single yeast cells under a microscope.
79424.m: Yeast is made of tiny living fungi.

79425.q: What do the yeast fungi in dough like to eat most?
79425.e: Yeast fungi feed on sugar. As they do, they make gas that puffs up the dough.

79426.q: What makes a yeast dough rise?
79426.e: The yeast fungi make lots of gas bubbles in the dough. This gas makes the dough big and airy.
79426.m: Yeast makes the dough rise with gas.

79427.q: Where does a yeast dough rise fastest?
79427.e: Yeast likes it warm. In a warm place the yeast fungi work quickly, in the cold only slowly.
79427.m: Yeast dough rises quickly in the warmth.

79428.q: What happens to yeast when it gets very hot?
79428.e: Yeast is made of living things. In great heat they die, for example in the hot oven during baking.

79429.q: Which Swiss Sunday bake is made with yeast?
79429.e: Zopf, a plaited loaf, is made with yeast. The yeast makes it nice and soft and airy.

79430.q: What do you call the process in which yeast makes gas and a little alcohol?
79430.e: This process is called fermentation. The gas makes the dough rise, and the alcohol evaporates during baking.

79431.q: In what form do you often buy fresh yeast in the shop?
79431.e: Fresh yeast is usually sold as a small cube. Dried yeast comes as a powder in a sachet.
79431.m: Fresh yeast is bought as a cube.

79432.e: Vinegar contains an acid. That is why it tastes sour.

79433.q: What is vinegar often used for in the kitchen?
79433.e: Vinegar gives salad dressing a sour taste. It is usually mixed with oil and spices.
79433.m: Vinegar is used for salad dressing.

79434.e: The acetic acid evaporates easily and stings the nose. That is why vinegar smells sharp and sour.

79435.q: What can you remove from a kettle with vinegar?
79435.e: The acid in vinegar dissolves limescale. That is why diluted vinegar helps against white limescale rings.

79436.q: What is cider vinegar made from?
79436.e: Cider vinegar is made from apple juice or cider. This slowly turns sour.
79436.m: Cider vinegar is made from apples.

79437.q: Which tiny living things turn wine into vinegar?
79437.e: Acetic acid bacteria turn the alcohol in wine into acetic acid. This is how wine vinegar is made.

79438.q: Why are gherkins pickled in vinegar?
a: So they go soft like mush
79438.e: The acid in vinegar stops many germs. So pickled gherkins stay good to eat for a long time.

79439.q: What happens to the shell of a raw egg that lies in vinegar for days?
79439.e: The acid in vinegar attacks the hard shell. After a few days only the thin skin is left, and the egg is soft like a rubber ball.

79440.q: What do you often get after eating something very salty?
79440.e: The body has to balance a lot of salt in food with water. That is why you are often very thirsty after salty food.

79441.q: Where does most of the salt in Switzerland come from?
79441.e: Deep underground in Switzerland there are ancient layers of salt. The salt is dissolved out with water, and then the water is evaporated.

79442.q: In which place in the canton of Vaud can you visit an old salt mine?
79442.e: Salt has been mined in Bex for centuries. Visitors can ride into the mine on a little train.
79442.m: There is a salt mine in Bex.

79443.q: Why do you add a pinch of salt to the water for cooking pasta?
79443.e: The pasta takes up a little salt while cooking. That makes it taste more flavourful.
79443.m: Salt in the cooking water gives pasta flavour.

79444.q: What do grains of salt look like under a magnifying glass?
79444.e: Table salt forms cube-shaped crystals. With a magnifying glass you can see the little cubes well.
79444.m: Grains of salt are little cubes.

79445.q: Why is salt spread on icy roads in winter?
79445.e: Salt makes ice melt even in the cold. This makes roads and pavements less slippery.

79446.q: Which substance is added to table salt in Switzerland to keep the thyroid healthy?
79446.e: The body needs iodine for the thyroid gland. That is why Switzerland has had iodised table salt for over 100 years.

79447.q: What do you knead salt dough for crafts from?
79447.e: Salt dough is kneaded from flour, salt and water. After drying or baking it goes hard, and you can paint it.
79447.m: Salt dough is made from flour, salt and water.

79448.q: Which plant is sugar made from in Switzerland?
79448.e: In Switzerland, sugar beet grows in many fields. Sugar is made from its juice.
79448.m: Swiss sugar comes from sugar beet.

79449.q: In which place in the canton of Bern is there a large Swiss sugar factory?
79449.e: Sugar has been made in Aarberg for over 100 years. A second sugar factory is in Frauenfeld.
79449.m: There is a sugar factory in Aarberg.

79450.q: What happens if you stir a lot of sugar into a small glass of water?
79450.e: Water can only dissolve a certain amount of sugar. Anything extra stays at the bottom as grains.
79450.m: Water cannot dissolve endless amounts of sugar.

79451.q: Which plant is much sugar made from in warm countries?
79451.e: Sugar cane is a tall grass that grows in warm countries. Its stalks are full of sweet juice.
79451.m: In warm countries, sugar is made from sugar cane.

79452.q: Which sugar is as fine as flour?
79452.e: Icing sugar is very finely ground sugar. It is used for dusting or for icing.
79452.m: Icing sugar is as fine as flour.

79453.q: What can lots of sweets cause in your teeth?
79453.e: Bacteria in the mouth turn sugar into acid. This acid can attack the teeth and cause tooth decay.
79453.m: Too much sugar can cause tooth decay.

79454.q: What is sugar pressed into little blocks called?
79454.e: Sugar cubes are made of pressed sugar crystals. This makes them easy to count.

79455.e: Green leaves make sugar with sunlight, water and air. The plant stores it, for example, in fruits or roots.
79455.m: Plants make sugar in their green leaves.

79456.q: What do you get when a machine spins melted sugar into fine threads?
79456.e: The machine melts sugar and spins it through tiny holes. The threads set at once and form a cloud.
79456.m: Candyfloss is made of fine sugar threads.

79457.q: What do you sprinkle on crème brûlée before browning it with a flame?
79457.e: Under the hot flame, the sugar melts and turns brown. This makes a crunchy crust on top.
79457.m: Sugar is sprinkled on crème brûlée.

79458.q: What is melted brown sugar called?
79458.e: When sugar is heated strongly, it melts and turns brown. This is called caramel.
79458.m: Brown, melted sugar is called caramel.

79459.q: What does sugar smell like when it caramelises?
79459.e: When sugar caramelises, new scents are formed. That is why it smells sweet and slightly toasted.

79460.q: What happens if you heat caramel for far too long?
79460.e: Sugar heated for too long burns. Then it turns black and tastes bitter.
79460.m: Caramel that gets too hot burns and turns bitter.

79461.q: Why is liquid caramel in the pan dangerous?
a: It is hotter than boiling water
79461.e: Caramel only forms well above 100 degrees. It sticks to the skin and burns it badly.

79462.q: Which Swiss dessert has a caramel sauce?
79462.e: Caramelköpfli is a pudding with a brown caramel sauce. You turn it out onto a plate.

79463.q: What happens to liquid caramel when it cools down?
79463.e: As it cools, liquid caramel sets and becomes as hard as glass. This is how hard sweets are made.

79464.q: Which fairground treat has a coating of caramel?
79464.e: Caramelised almonds are heated with sugar in a pan. The sugar caramelises and coats the almonds.
79464.m: Caramelised almonds have a caramel coating.

79465.q: Which Swiss sweet is made by boiling sugar and cream until it is light brown?
79465.e: For Rahmtäfeli, sugar is boiled with cream and butter. The sugar caramelises and turns the mixture brown.
79465.m: Rahmtäfeli are made from sugar and cream.

79466.q: Why does a cut apple with lemon juice turn brown more slowly?
a: The juice slows down the browning
79466.e: In the air, the flesh of the fruit turns brown. Lemon juice slows this change down.
79466.m: Lemon juice keeps apples pale for longer.

79467.q: Which vitamin is lemon juice especially rich in?
79467.e: Lemons are rich in vitamin C. The body needs it, for example, to fight off illness.
79467.m: Lemons contain a lot of vitamin C.

79468.q: What happens when you pour lemon juice into milk?
79468.e: The acid in the lemon makes the protein in the milk clump together. White flakes form.

79469.q: What happens to a dark, tarnished copper coin when you rub it with lemon juice and salt?
79469.e: The acid in lemon juice dissolves the dark layer on the coin. The shiny metal underneath appears again.
79469.m: Lemon juice makes dark copper shiny again.

79470.q: Where in a lemon is the strong-smelling oil?
79470.e: The lemon peel contains tiny oil glands. If you grate the peel, it smells strongly of lemon.
79470.m: The scented oil is in the lemon peel.

79471.q: What can you produce with a lemon, a piece of copper and a piece of zinc?
79471.e: The sour juice and the two metals together form a simple battery. It supplies a tiny bit of electricity.
79471.m: You can build a battery with a lemon.

79472.q: Which group of fruits does the lemon belong to?
79472.e: The lemon belongs to the citrus fruits. Oranges and mandarins are citrus fruits too.
79472.m: The lemon is a citrus fruit.

79473.q: What happens when you drip lemon juice onto a piece of limestone?
a: The stone goes soft like wax
79473.e: The acid in lemon juice attacks the limestone. This produces a gas that forms little bubbles.

79474.q: What happens when you pour sherbet powder into water?
79474.e: In water, the substances in the sherbet powder react with each other. This forms lots of gas bubbles.

79475.q: Which two substances in sherbet powder fizz together?
a: Bicarbonate of soda and an acid
79475.e: Sherbet powder contains bicarbonate of soda and an acid. Together with water they make gas.
79475.m: Bicarbonate of soda and acid make sherbet powder fizz.

79476.q: Which acid is often found in sherbet powder?
79476.e: Sherbet powder usually contains citric acid or tartaric acid. It also gives the slightly sour taste.
79476.m: Sherbet powder often contains citric acid.

79477.q: What do you feel when you sprinkle sherbet powder on your tongue?
79477.e: Saliva is moist. That is why the sherbet powder starts to fizz and tingle on your tongue.
79477.m: Sherbet powder tingles on the tongue.

79478.q: Why must sherbet powder be kept dry?
a: Otherwise it fizzes in the tin
79478.e: Moisture starts the reaction. Then the powder is used up before you put it in the glass.

79479.q: What is a pressed tablet that fizzes in water called?
79479.e: An effervescent tablet contains the same substances as sherbet powder. It is just pressed tightly together.

79480.e: Besides bicarbonate of soda and acid, sherbet powder contains sugar. It gives the sweet taste.

79481.q: Where does sherbet powder fizz faster, in warm or in cold water?
79481.e: In warm water, chemical reactions happen faster. That is why sherbet powder fizzes more strongly there and is finished sooner.
79481.m: Sherbet powder fizzes faster in warm water.

79482.e: Lactic acid bacteria eat the milk sugar. As they do, they make acid, and the milk goes sour.

79483.q: Which acid forms in soured milk?
79483.e: The bacteria turn the milk sugar into lactic acid. This acid gets its name from milk (Latin ‘lac’).
79483.m: Lactic acid forms in soured milk.

79484.q: How does milk change when it goes sour?
79484.e: The acid makes the protein in the milk curdle. That is why soured milk gets thicker.

79485.q: Which dairy product is made with the help of lactic acid bacteria?
79485.e: To make yoghurt, lactic acid bacteria are added to warm milk. They make the milk sour and thick.
79485.m: Yoghurt is made with lactic acid bacteria.

79486.q: Where does milk go sour fastest?
79486.e: Bacteria multiply quickly in the warmth. In the fridge they work only slowly.
79486.m: Milk goes sour quickly in the warmth.

79487.q: What does soured milk taste like?
79487.e: Soured milk contains lactic acid. That is why it tastes slightly sour.

79488.q: What do you get when you let soured, thick milk drain?
79488.e: As it drains, the liquid runs away. A thick, white mass is left behind: quark.
79488.m: Quark is made from soured milk.

79489.q: What is the yellowish liquid that separates from soured milk called?
79489.e: When milk curdles, a yellowish liquid separates off. This liquid is called whey.
79489.m: The liquid from curdled milk is called whey.

79490.q: What happens to egg white when it is cooked?
79490.e: Raw egg white is see-through and runny. The heat makes it white and firm.
79490.m: Cooked egg white turns white and firm.

79491.q: About how long do you boil a hard-boiled egg?
79491.e: A medium egg is hard after about 10 minutes in boiling water. A soft-boiled egg needs only about 5 minutes.
79491.m: A hard-boiled egg boils for about 10 minutes.

79492.q: Can you make a boiled egg raw again?
79492.e: When cooked, the egg white changes for ever. This change cannot be undone.
79492.m: A boiled egg never becomes raw again.

79493.q: How does a hard-boiled egg spin on the table?
79493.e: Everything inside a hard-boiled egg is solid, so it spins like a top. A raw egg wobbles because the inside sloshes about.
79493.m: A hard-boiled egg spins like a top.

79494.q: Why do you put eggs in cold water after boiling them?
a: So they take in more salt
79494.e: A hot egg keeps cooking even outside the pan. Cold water cools it down quickly.

79495.q: What does the yolk get if you boil an egg for far too long?
79495.e: If boiled too long, substances from the white and the yolk react with each other. This produces a greenish rim.
79495.m: Eggs boiled too long have a green rim.

79496.q: Why are eggs often pricked before boiling?
79496.e: There is a small air bubble inside an egg. Through the hole, the air can escape when heated, and the shell cracks less often.

79497.q: Which sets first when cooking, the egg white or the yolk?
79497.e: The egg white is on the outside and gets hot first. It also sets at a slightly lower temperature than the yolk.
79497.m: When cooking, the egg white sets first.

79498.q: Which cereal is popcorn made from?
79498.e: Popcorn is made from a special kind of maize. The kernels burst open when heated.

79499.q: What is inside a maize kernel that turns to steam when heated?
79499.e: Inside the kernel there is some water. When heated, it turns into hot steam.
79499.m: A maize kernel contains a little water.

79500.q: Why does a maize kernel burst open when heated?
a: The kernel is cut from the outside
The oil presses from the outside
79500.e: The steam inside the kernel presses harder and harder against the hard shell. At some point it suddenly splits open.
79500.m: Steam bursts the maize kernel open.

79501.q: What is the kind of maize used to make popcorn called?
79501.e: Popping corn has an especially hard shell. That is why enough pressure can build up inside.
79501.m: Popcorn is made from popping corn.

79502.q: Why does a maize kernel with a crack in its shell not pop properly?
79502.e: The steam can slowly escape through the crack. So no pressure builds up to burst the kernel.
79502.m: A kernel with a crack does not pop properly.

79503.q: What do you hear when popcorn pops in the pan?
79503.e: Each kernel bursts open with a small bang. That is why the pan keeps popping.
79503.m: Popcorn pops as it bursts open.

79504.q: How does a maize kernel change when it becomes popcorn?
79504.e: When it bursts, the soft inside of the kernel puffs up. The popcorn is much bigger than the kernel was before.
79504.m: Popcorn is much bigger than the maize kernel.

79505.q: Where does maize originally come from?
79505.e: Maize was first grown in Central America. Only later did it come to Europe.

79506.q: Why do you put a lid on the pan when making popcorn?
a: So the kernels don't jump out
79506.e: The bursting kernels jump up. With the lid they stay in the pan, and hot oil does not spatter out.
79506.m: A lid keeps the popcorn in the pan.

79507.q: Which parts of the sunflower is sunflower oil pressed from?
79507.e: Sunflower seeds contain a lot of oil. It is pressed out in an oil mill.
79507.m: Sunflower oil comes from the seeds.

79508.q: Which yellow-flowering field crop is most home-grown cooking oil in Switzerland pressed from?
79508.e: In spring, many rapeseed fields bloom yellow in Switzerland. Rapeseed oil is pressed from the small seeds.
79508.m: A lot of rapeseed oil is made in Switzerland.

79509.q: Which oil is made from the fruit of trees around the Mediterranean?
79509.e: Olive trees grow mainly around the Mediterranean. Olive oil is pressed from their fruit.

79510.q: What does a drop of oil leave on paper?
79510.e: Oil soaks into the paper and does not evaporate like water. That is why a see-through grease spot is left.
79510.m: Oil leaves a grease spot on paper.

79511.q: Why is cooking oil best kept in a dark, cool place?
79511.e: Light, warmth and air change the oil over time. Then it smells and tastes rancid.
79511.m: Keep cooking oil dark and cool.

79512.q: What does oil feel like between your fingers?
79512.e: Oil makes the skin smooth and slippery. That is why it feels slippery.

79513.q: Where should old cooking oil go?
79513.e: Oil blocks pipes and pollutes water. That is why you take it to a collection point in a bottle.
79513.m: Old oil goes to a collection point.

79514.q: What often happens to olive oil in the fridge?
79514.e: In the cold, some fats in olive oil go solid. That is why it goes cloudy and thick, but clear again when warm.
79514.m: Olive oil goes cloudy in the cold.

79515.e: Chips are deep-fried in hot oil. The oil is much hotter than boiling water and makes them crispy.
79515.m: Chips are fried in hot oil.

79715.q: Which six letters does the top row of letters on a Swiss keyboard start with?
79715.e: The Swiss keyboard is called a QWERTZ keyboard after its first letters. In America it is QWERTY, in France AZERTY.
79715.m: In Switzerland people type on a QWERTZ keyboard.

79716.q: Which key do you press to start a new line?
79716.e: The Enter key, also called the Return key, starts a new line in a text.
79716.m: The Enter key starts a new line.

79717.q: Which key do you use to delete the letter to the left of the blinking line?
79717.e: The Backspace key has an arrow pointing left. It deletes the character to the left of the blinking line.
79717.m: The Backspace key deletes to the left.

79718.q: What is the blinking line called that shows where the next letter will appear?
79718.e: The blinking line is called the cursor. The next character you type appears there.
79718.m: The cursor shows where you are writing.

79719.q: Which letters with dots does the Swiss keyboard have for German?
79719.e: The Swiss keyboard has its own keys for ä, ö and ü. There is no separate character for the German sharp S, because in Switzerland people write “ss”.
79719.m: The Swiss keyboard has keys for ä, ö and ü.

79720.q: What is the block on the right of many keyboards that only has numbers called?
79720.e: Many large keyboards have a number pad on the right. There the numbers are arranged as on a calculator.
79720.m: The number pad helps you type numbers quickly.

79721.q: Which keys do you use to move the cursor up, down, left and right?
79721.e: The four arrow keys point in four directions. You use them to move the cursor in the text.
79721.m: The arrow keys move the cursor.

79722.q: Which fingers do you put on the keys when touch typing?
79722.e: In touch typing you type with all ten fingers. That way you write faster and do not have to look at the keys as much.
79722.m: In touch typing, all your fingers type.

79723.q: Which key at the top left often cancels something on the computer?
79723.e: The Esc key is at the top left. “Esc” comes from the English word “escape”. You use it to leave full screen, for example.
79723.m: You often cancel something with the Esc key.

79724.q: Why is the computer mouse called a “mouse”?
a: The cable looks like a tail
It used to always be grey
79724.e: The first mice had a cable at the back. Their shape and size were like a small mouse, and the cable was like its tail.
79724.m: The mouse gets its name from its shape with the cable.

79725.q: Which mouse button do you usually click with?
79725.e: For normal clicks you use the left mouse button. The right button opens a small menu.
79725.m: Normally you click with the left mouse button.

79726.q: What does a click with the right mouse button usually open?
79726.e: The right mouse button opens a context menu. It lists things you can do with what you clicked on.
79726.m: The right mouse button opens a menu.

79727.q: What is the little wheel between the mouse buttons for?
79727.e: If you turn the mouse wheel, the page on the screen moves up or down. This is called scrolling.
79727.m: With the mouse wheel you scroll through a page.

79728.q: What do you call moving a picture to another place while holding down the mouse button?
79728.e: You click on something, hold the button down, pull it away and let go. This is called drag and drop.
79728.m: When you drag and drop, you hold the mouse button down.

79729.q: What do you often put the mouse on so that it glides well?
79729.e: A mouse mat is a flat surface. The mouse glides well on it and the sensor detects the movement reliably.
79729.m: A mouse mat is the surface for the mouse.

79730.q: What does a laptop often have instead of a mouse?
79730.e: A touchpad is a smooth surface below the keyboard. When you move your finger on it, the pointer moves.
79730.m: On a laptop, the touchpad often replaces the mouse.

79731.q: What do you need for a wireless mouse without a cable?
79731.e: A wireless mouse has no cable and so gets no power from the computer. It needs batteries or a rechargeable battery.
79731.m: A mouse without a cable needs its own power source.

79732.q: What happens to the mouse pointer when you push the mouse to the right?
79732.e: The pointer follows the movement of the mouse. If you push the mouse to the right, the pointer moves to the right too.
79732.m: The mouse pointer moves like the mouse.

79733.q: What is another word for a computer screen?
79733.e: A computer's screen is also called a monitor.
79733.m: A monitor is a computer screen.

79734.q: What is the area with the little pictures that you see after starting the computer called?
79734.e: The desktop is the work area on the screen. Small pictures for programs and folders are on it.
79734.m: The desktop is the computer's work area.

79735.q: What is the picture you see in the background of the desktop called?
79735.e: The picture behind all the windows and icons is called the wallpaper. You can choose it yourself.
79735.m: You can choose the wallpaper yourself.

79736.q: Roughly how far should your eyes be from the screen?
79736.e: Experts recommend a distance of about an arm's length from the screen. This is easier on the eyes.
79736.m: Keep about an arm's length away from the screen.

79737.q: What is good for your eyes when you look at a screen for a long time?
a: Taking breaks and looking into the distance
79737.e: Breaks and looking into the distance relax the eyes. Looking at the screen for a long time without a break makes your eyes tired.
79737.m: Short breaks are good for your eyes.

79738.q: What is the best thing to clean a screen with?
79738.e: A soft, dry or slightly damp cloth cleans the screen without scratches. Too much water can damage the device.
79738.m: A soft cloth protects the screen.

79739.q: What is the setting called that makes a screen lighter or darker?
79739.e: With brightness you set how strongly the screen shines.
79739.m: Brightness makes the screen lighter or darker.

79740.q: What is the picture called that appears when the computer has not been used for a while?
79740.e: If the computer is not used for some time, it often shows a screen saver or turns the screen dark.
79740.m: The screen saver appears during a break.

79741.q: What is the small camera at the top of the screen for video calls called?
79741.e: A webcam is a small camera on or in the screen. It lets people see you during video calls.
79741.m: The webcam lets people see you in video calls.

79742.q: Which printer prints with tiny drops of ink?
79742.e: An inkjet printer sprays tiny drops of ink onto the paper.
79742.m: The inkjet printer prints with ink.

79743.q: What does an inkjet printer need when the ink runs out?
79743.e: The ink is in cartridges. When a cartridge is empty, you put in a new one.
79743.m: Empty ink cartridges have to be replaced.

79744.q: What is the fine colour powder a laser printer prints with called?
79744.e: A laser printer uses a fine colour powder. It is called toner and is fixed onto the paper with heat.
79744.m: A laser printer prints with toner.

79745.q: Which printer can make real objects out of plastic?
79745.e: A 3D printer builds objects layer by layer, often from melted plastic.

79746.q: What does the print preview show?
a: What the sheet will look like
79746.e: In the print preview you see before printing what the page will look like on paper. That way you save paper.
79746.m: The print preview shows the sheet before printing.

79747.q: What is the device called that reads a sheet of paper into the computer?
79747.e: A scanner makes a picture of a sheet and sends it to the computer. The printer does the opposite.
79747.m: The scanner reads paper into the computer.

79748.q: How do you save paper when printing?
79748.e: If you only print what you really need, you save paper, ink and electricity.
79748.m: Only print what you really need.

79749.q: What happens with a paper jam in the printer?
79749.e: In a paper jam, a sheet gets stuck in the printer. Then you have to pull it out carefully.
79749.m: In a paper jam, a sheet is stuck.

79750.q: What do you use headphones on the computer for?
a: To hear sounds on your own
79750.e: With headphones you hear sounds right at your ear. That way you do not disturb other people.
79750.m: With headphones you can listen without disturbing others.

79751.q: Why should you not listen too loudly with headphones?
79751.e: Very loud sounds right at the ear can damage your hearing over time. That is why you set the volume pleasantly low.
79751.m: Music that is too loud harms your ears.

79752.q: What are headphones with a built-in microphone called?
79752.e: A headset is headphones with a microphone. With it you can listen and speak, for example in a video call.
79752.m: A headset comes with a microphone.

79753.q: What are very small headphones that you put straight into your ear called?
79753.e: Small headphones that go in the ear are called earphones or in-ear headphones.
79753.m: You put earphones into your ear.

79754.q: Which wireless technology do many headphones use to connect without a cable?
79754.e: Many wireless headphones connect to the computer, tablet or mobile phone via Bluetooth.
79754.m: Wireless headphones often connect via Bluetooth.

79755.q: What do L and R on the sides of headphones stand for?
79755.e: L stands for left and R for right. That way you put the headphones on correctly.
79755.m: On headphones, L stands for left and R for right.

79756.q: Why should you not wear loud headphones in traffic?
a: You cannot hear cars and bikes
79756.e: With loud music in your ears, you hear cars, bikes or warning signals badly. That is dangerous.
79756.m: In traffic you must be able to hear well.

79757.q: Where do you plug headphones with a cable into the computer?
79757.e: Headphones with a cable have a small plug. It goes into the headphone socket on the computer or screen.
79757.m: Headphones with a cable plug into the headphone socket.

79758.q: What do you do when you double-click?
a: Press once for a long time
79758.e: When you double-click, you press the left mouse button twice briefly, one right after the other.
79758.m: A double-click is two quick clicks.

79759.q: What usually happens when you double-click a program icon?
79759.e: A double-click on an icon usually opens the program, file or folder.
79759.m: You open something with a double-click.

79760.q: Where can you set how fast a double-click has to be?
79760.e: In the mouse settings you can change the double-click speed. Then it also works with slower clicks.
79760.m: You set the double-click speed in the mouse settings.

79761.q: What happens if the two clicks are too slow?
a: It does not count as a double-click
79761.e: If the two clicks are too far apart, the computer sees two single clicks. Then nothing opens.
79761.m: For a double-click you have to click quickly.

79762.q: What does a double-click on a folder open?
79762.e: If you double-click a folder, you see what is saved in it.
79762.m: A double-click on a folder shows its contents.

79763.q: What does a single click on an icon usually do?
79763.e: A single click only selects the icon. Only a double-click opens it.

79764.q: What does a double-click on a word in a text often do?
79764.e: In many writing programs, a double-click selects a whole word.
79764.m: A double-click selects a whole word.

79765.q: How do you double-click on a touchpad?
79765.e: On the touchpad you tap twice quickly with your finger. That works like a double-click.
79765.m: On a touchpad you tap twice for a double-click.

79766.q: What is an icon on the computer?
79766.e: An icon is a small picture on the screen. It stands for a program, a file or a folder.
79766.m: An icon is a small picture for something on the computer.

79768.q: What does the print icon usually look like?
79768.e: The print icon usually shows a small printer. That way you recognise it without words.
79768.m: The picture shows what an icon does.

79769.q: What does an icon with a magnifying glass often stand for?
79769.e: You look closely with a magnifying glass. That is why the magnifying glass icon usually stands for searching.
79769.m: The magnifying glass icon stands for searching.

79770.q: What does an icon with a cog often stand for?
79770.e: The cog stands for technology. With this icon you usually open the settings.
79770.m: The cog icon opens the settings.

79771.q: What does an icon with a small house often stand for?
79771.e: The house icon usually takes you back to the home page, so back home.
79771.m: The house icon takes you to the home page.

79772.q: What does an icon with a loudspeaker often stand for?
79772.e: With the loudspeaker icon you set how loud the computer is.
79772.m: You set the volume with the loudspeaker icon.

79773.q: What does an icon with a floppy disk often stand for?
79773.e: In the past, people saved files on floppy disks. That is why the floppy disk icon still stands for saving today.
79773.m: The floppy disk icon stands for saving.

79774.q: How do you close a program window on Windows?
a: With the X at the top right
79774.e: At the top right of a window there is an X. Clicking on it closes the window.
79774.m: You close a window with the X.

79775.q: What is the top bar of a window with the name of the program called?
79775.e: Right at the top of the window, the title bar shows the name of the program or file.
79775.m: The title bar shows the name of the window.

79776.q: What does the button with the small line at the top right of a window do?
79776.e: The line minimises the window. It disappears from the screen but stays open.

79777.q: What happens if you maximise a window?
79777.e: Maximising means making it big. The window becomes as big as the whole screen.
79777.m: A maximised window is the size of the screen.

79778.q: How do you move a window to another place?
a: Drag it by the title bar
79778.e: You click on the title bar, hold the mouse button down and drag the window to the new place.
79778.m: You move windows by the title bar.

79779.q: What is the bar at the bottom of the Windows screen with the open programs called?
79779.e: At the bottom of the screen is the taskbar. There you can see which programs are open.
79779.m: In the taskbar you see the open programs.

79780.q: Can you have several program windows open at the same time?
a: Yes, lots at the same time
79780.e: A computer can have many windows open at once. They lie on top of each other like sheets of paper on a table.
79780.m: Many windows can be open on a computer.

79781.q: What is the bar at the edge of a window called that you use to move through a long text?
79781.e: With the scroll bar at the edge, you move the contents of a window up or down.
79781.m: The scroll bar shows more of the contents.

79782.q: Which window is active when several are open?
79782.e: The window you clicked on last is at the front and active. That is where what you type ends up.
79782.m: The window you clicked on is at the front.

79783.q: What do you need folders on the computer for?
79783.e: In folders you collect files that belong together. That way you find them again more quickly.
79783.m: Folders bring order to your files.

79784.q: What colour is the folder icon on Windows usually?
79784.e: On Windows, a folder usually looks like a yellow file folder.
79784.m: On Windows, folders are usually yellow.

79785.q: Which name does a new folder get first on Windows?
79785.e: When you create a folder, it is first called “New folder”. Then you can give it a name of your own.
79785.m: Give a new folder a suitable name.

79786.q: What do you call giving a folder a new name?
79786.e: Renaming a folder means giving it a different name.
79786.m: When renaming, a folder gets a new name.

79787.q: Which name is best for a folder with photos from ski camp?
79787.e: A good folder name says what is in it. You will find “Ski camp photos” again straight away later.
79787.m: A good folder name says what is in it.

79788.q: How do you move a file into a folder?
a: Drag it in with the mouse
79788.e: You drag the file onto the folder with the mouse button held down and let go. Then it is in the folder.
79788.m: You can drag files into folders with the mouse.

79789.q: What happens to the files if you delete a folder?
79789.e: If you delete a folder, you also delete everything in it. That is why you look inside first.
79789.m: When a folder goes, its contents go too.

79790.q: Where do you find a ready-made folder for pictures on many computers?
79790.e: Many computers already have ready-made folders such as “Pictures”, “Documents” or “Music”.
79790.m: Many computers already have a folder for pictures.

79791.q: Which key on the keyboard is the longest?
79791.e: The space bar is the long key right at the bottom in the middle. It is the longest key.
79791.m: The space bar is the longest key.

79792.q: What does the space bar do when you are writing?
79792.e: With the space bar you put a gap between two words.
79792.m: Between words you press the space bar.

79793.q: Which finger do you press the space bar with when touch typing?
79793.e: Your thumbs rest above the space bar. That is why you press it with a thumb.
79793.m: You press the space bar with your thumb.

79794.q: Where is the space bar on the keyboard?
a: At the bottom in the middle
79794.e: The space bar is in the bottom row in the middle. That way both thumbs can reach it.
79794.m: The space bar is at the bottom in the middle.

79795.q: What happens in many video programs when you press the space bar?
a: The video pauses or carries on
79795.e: In many video and music programs, the space bar switches back and forth between play and pause.
79795.m: In many videos, the space bar starts and stops.

79796.q: How many spaces do you normally put between two words?
79796.e: There is normally exactly one space between two words.
79796.m: There is one space between words.

79797.q: Which key do you press to jump in many computer games?
79797.e: In many games, the character jumps when you press the space bar. It is big and easy to hit.
79797.m: In many games you jump with the space bar.

79799.q: What do you press the Shift key for when writing?
79799.e: If you hold the Shift key down and type a letter, it is written as a capital.
79799.m: With the Shift key you write capitals.

79800.q: Which symbol is often on the Shift key?
79800.e: The Shift key usually shows a wide arrow pointing up.
79800.m: The Shift key shows an arrow pointing up.

79802.q: How many Shift keys does a normal keyboard have?
79802.e: A normal keyboard has one Shift key on the left and one on the right. That way you can write capitals with both hands.
79802.m: There is a Shift key on the left and on the right.

79803.q: Which character do you get on a Swiss keyboard with Shift and the key 1?
79803.e: On the Swiss keyboard, the plus sign is above the 1. With Shift and 1 you write +.
79803.m: The Shift key gives you the upper character on a key.

79804.q: Which key writes capitals all the time until you press it again?
79804.e: The Caps Lock key locks in place. Then you write all letters as capitals until you press it once more.
79804.m: The Caps Lock key writes capitals all the time.

79805.q: What do you have to do to write a capital A with the Shift key?
a: Hold it down and type A
Let go of it and wait
79805.e: You hold the Shift key down and type the A at the same time. Then you let go of both.
79805.m: You hold the Shift key down while typing.

79806.q: Which character do you get on a Swiss keyboard with Shift and the key 7?
79806.e: On the Swiss keyboard, the slash is above the 7. With Shift and 7 you write /.
79806.m: You reach many characters with the Shift key.

79807.q: How do you switch a computer off properly?
79807.e: When shutting down, the computer closes all programs properly and then switches itself off.
79807.m: You shut a computer down before it is off.

79808.q: Why should you not just pull out the plug?
79808.e: If you just pull out the plug, unsaved work can be lost. Files can also be damaged.
79808.m: Only pull out the plug after shutting down.

79809.q: What should you do before shutting down?
79809.e: Before shutting down, you save your work. That way it is still there next time.
79809.m: Save your work before shutting down.

79810.q: Where do you find the command for shutting down on Windows?
79810.e: On Windows you click on the Start menu and then on the power symbol. There you can shut down.
79810.m: On Windows you shut down through the Start menu.

79811.q: What does the power symbol usually look like?
a: A circle with a line at the top
79811.e: The power symbol is an open circle with a short line at the top. You find it on many devices.
79811.m: The circle with the line is the power symbol.

79812.q: What is it called when the computer goes off and comes straight back on?
79812.e: When restarting, the computer shuts down and starts again immediately. This often helps when something is not working properly.
79812.m: A restart often helps with small problems.

79813.q: What is the state called in which the computer sleeps but is quickly ready again?
79813.e: In sleep mode the computer uses only a little electricity. It wakes up again quickly.
79813.m: In sleep mode the computer is only asleep.

79814.q: Why do you shut the computer down in the evening?
79814.e: A computer that is switched off uses no electricity. This is good for the environment and your wallet.
79814.m: A computer that is switched off saves electricity.

80015.q: What do you say about someone who is especially good at making plants grow?
80015.e: “Having green fingers” is a saying. It is said about people who are good with plants.
80015.m: If you have green fingers, you are good at gardening.

80016.q: How many finger bones (sections) does the thumb have?
80016.e: The thumb has only two sections. That is why it is shorter than most of the other fingers.

80017.q: Which finger can touch the tips of all the other fingers on the same hand?
80017.e: You can place your thumb opposite the other fingers. That way you can grip well, for example a pencil or a spoon.
80017.m: With the thumb you can grip well.

80018.q: What does it usually mean when someone gives a thumbs up?
80018.e: A thumbs up is a sign for “good” or “everything's fine” here.

80019.q: What are you wishing someone when you keep your fingers crossed for them?
80019.e: “I'll keep my fingers crossed for you” is a saying. You use it to wish someone lots of luck. In German-speaking countries people press their thumbs instead.
80019.m: Keeping your fingers crossed means wishing luck.

80020.q: Which finger do many babies like to suck?
80020.e: Many babies suck their thumb. It calms them, and some even do it before they are born.

80021.q: What is the name of the tiny girl in Hans Christian Andersen's fairy tale who is only as big as a thumb?
80021.e: In the fairy tale “Thumbelina”, a tiny girl has lots of adventures. Her name comes from the word thumb.
80021.m: Thumbelina is only as big as a thumb.

a: A little book of pictures that move when you flick through it
A very small cinema for mice
80022.e: With a flip book you let the pages run quickly past your thumb. The pictures then look as if they are moving.
80022.m: A flip book turns lots of pictures into a little film.

80023.q: What does a hitchhiker at the side of the road show with their thumb?
a: That they would like a lift
That they are showing the way
80023.e: Hitchhikers hold their thumb out in the direction of travel. That way they show drivers that they would like a lift.
80023.m: With their thumb, a hitchhiker shows that they want a lift.

80024.q: Which finger is right next to the thumb?
80024.e: Next to the thumb comes the index finger. It is the second finger of the hand.
80024.m: The index finger is next to the thumb.

80025.q: Which finger do you usually point at something with?
80025.e: The index finger is also called the pointing finger. You use it to point at things or directions.
80025.m: You point at things with your index finger.

80026.q: Which finger do many children stick up at school when they want to answer?
80026.e: If you want to say something, you put up your hand and often stretch your index finger up. That way the teacher can see who wants to speak.
80026.m: When you put your hand up, you often stretch up your index finger.

80027.q: What does someone mean who holds their index finger in front of their lips?
80027.e: The index finger in front of the lips means “shh”. You use it to ask others to be quiet.
80027.m: A finger in front of the lips means “Be quiet!”.

80029.q: What does someone often mean when they raise their index finger while talking?
80029.e: A raised index finger is a warning. It means that someone should be careful or listen.
80029.m: A raised index finger is a warning.

80030.q: How many sections does the index finger have?
80030.e: The index finger has three sections. The middle finger, ring finger and little finger have just as many.
80030.m: The index finger has three sections.

80031.q: Which finger do many children run along under the line when they are learning to read?
80031.e: When you are learning to read, your index finger helps you not to lose your place in the line. You follow along word by word.
80031.m: The index finger helps when you are learning to read.

80032.q: Which finger do you usually press a lift button with?
80032.e: The index finger is skilful and easy to control. That is why you usually press buttons and doorbells with it.
80032.m: You usually press buttons with your index finger.

80033.q: Which finger is the longest for most people?
80033.e: The middle finger is the longest finger for almost everyone. It is in the middle of the hand.
80033.m: The middle finger is the longest finger.

80034.q: Between which two fingers is the middle finger?
80034.e: The middle finger has a neighbour on each side. On one side is the index finger, on the other the ring finger.
80034.m: The middle finger is between the index finger and the ring finger.

80035.q: When playing the piano, each finger has a number, and the thumb is 1. Which number is the middle finger?
80035.e: You count from the thumb: thumb 1, index finger 2, middle finger 3. In piano music these numbers are written above the notes.
80035.m: On the piano, the middle finger is number 3.

80036.q: Which three fingers do people in Switzerland hold up when they swear an oath?
a: Thumb, index finger and middle finger
Index finger, ring finger and little finger
Thumb, ring finger and little finger
Middle finger, ring finger and little finger
80036.e: When swearing an oath, you raise your hand with the thumb, index finger and middle finger. The Rütli oath is often shown this way too.
80036.m: When swearing an oath, you hold up your thumb, index finger and middle finger.

80037.q: On which finger do many schoolchildren get a small hard patch from lots of writing?
80037.e: When you write, the pencil usually rests on the middle finger. The pressure can cause a small hard patch there.
80037.m: When you write, the pencil rests on the middle finger.

80038.q: On which finger do many married people wear their wedding ring?
80038.e: The wedding ring is usually worn on the ring finger. That is where this finger gets its name.
80038.m: You wear your wedding ring on your ring finger.

80039.q: Which finger is between the middle finger and the little finger?
80039.e: If you count from the thumb, the ring finger is the fourth finger. It is next to the little finger.
80039.m: The ring finger is the fourth finger.

80040.q: Which finger is the hardest to move completely on its own?
80040.e: The ring finger is closely connected to its neighbours by tendons. That is why they often move too when you try to straighten it alone.
80040.m: The ring finger is hard to move on its own.

80041.q: For many people, which finger is about the same length as the index finger?
80041.e: For many people, the index finger and ring finger are almost the same length. In some people one is a little longer, in others the other.
80041.m: The ring finger and index finger are often almost the same length.

80042.q: Which finger is the smallest on the hand?
80042.e: The little finger is the shortest and thinnest finger. Its name says it all.
80042.m: The little finger is the smallest finger.

80043.q: Which finger is right on the outside, on the opposite side of the hand from the thumb?
80043.e: The thumb is on one side and the little finger right on the other side. It is the fifth finger.
80043.m: The little finger is the fifth finger.

80044.q: How do many children make a really firm promise to each other?
a: They hook their little fingers together
80044.e: In a pinky promise, two children hook their little fingers together. It counts as an especially firm promise.
80044.m: With hooked little fingers you make a promise.

80045.q: How does the saying continue: “Give him an inch, ...”?
a: and he'll give you a foot
80045.e: The saying means: if you give someone a little, they immediately want much more.
80045.m: Give him an inch and he'll take a mile.

80046.q: In touch typing, which finger do you use to press the Enter key on the right of the keyboard?
80046.e: The Enter key is right on the outside on the right. That is why it is easiest to reach with your right little finger.
80046.m: You press the Enter key with your right little finger.

80047.q: How many little fingers does a person usually have?
80047.e: Each hand has one little finger. With two hands, that makes two.
80047.m: Each hand has one little finger.

80049.q: What is the inside of the hand called?
80049.e: The inside of the hand is called the palm. You use it to hold and grab things.
80049.m: The inside of the hand is called the palm.

80050.q: What never grows on the palm of your hand?
80050.e: The skin of the palm has no hair roots. That is why hair never grows there.
80050.m: No hair grows on the palm.

80051.q: What do you call the creases in the palm of your hand?
80051.e: Every palm has large creases, the palm lines. They help the skin to fold when you grip.
80051.m: The creases in the palm are called palm lines.

80052.q: What often happens to the palms of your hands when you are very nervous?
80052.e: There are very many sweat glands in the palm. When you are nervous, they often sweat and your hands get damp.
80052.m: When you are nervous, your hands often get sweaty.

80053.q: Which parts of your hands do you hit together when you clap?
80053.e: When you clap, your two palms meet. That makes the loud clapping sound.
80053.m: When you clap, you hit your palms together.

80054.q: What is the skin on the palm like compared with the back of the hand?
80054.e: The skin of the palm is thicker and tougher. That way it can cope with lots of rubbing and gripping.
80054.m: The skin of the palm is thick and tough.

80055.q: Which part of the hand is usually lighter than the rest in people with dark skin?
80055.e: The palm has less pigment in the skin. That is why, for many people, it is lighter than the back of the hand.
80055.m: The palm is often lighter than the rest of the hand.

80056.q: What do you call a hand shaped like a little bowl?
80056.e: If you shape your palm into a bowl, you get a cupped hand. You can scoop up water in it, for example.
80056.m: You can carry water in a cupped hand.

80057.q: Which part of your hand is best for catching a ball?
80057.e: The palm is soft and big. The ball lands in it, and the fingers close round it.
80057.m: You catch a ball with your palm.

80058.q: Who has exactly the same fingerprint as you?
80058.e: Every fingerprint is unique. Even identical twins have different fingerprints.
80058.m: Every person has their own fingerprint.

80059.q: Who looks for fingerprints at a crime scene?
80059.e: The police collect fingerprints at the crime scene. That way they can find out who was there.

80060.q: What can you see on a fingerprint?
80060.e: The skin of the fingertip has fine ridges. They form lines that you can see in the print.
80060.m: A fingerprint is made of fine lines.

80061.q: What happens to the pattern of your fingerprint as you get older?
80061.e: The pattern of a fingerprint stays the same for a whole lifetime. As you grow, it just gets bigger.
80061.m: The pattern of a fingerprint always stays the same.

80062.q: Which shape is a typical pattern in fingerprints?
80062.e: In fingerprints, there are mainly arches, loops and whorls. The loop is the most common pattern.
80062.m: Loops, arches and whorls are fingerprint patterns.

80063.q: Which animal has fingerprints that are very similar to human ones?
80063.e: Koalas have fingerprints that can hardly be told apart from human ones. They help them to grip branches.

80064.q: When does a person get their fingerprints?
80064.e: Fingerprints form while the baby is still growing in its mother's tummy. By birth they are finished.

80065.q: What can you use to unlock many mobile phones without typing in a number?
80065.e: Many phones have a sensor that recognises fingerprints. Because every print is different, the phone only opens for its owner.

80066.q: What has been stored on the chip of the Swiss passport since 2010?
80066.e: Since 2010 the Swiss passport has contained a chip. A photo and two fingerprints are stored on it.
80066.m: Two fingerprints are stored in the Swiss passport.

80067.q: How can you make your fingerprint clearly visible on paper?
a: Press your finger on an ink pad
Blow on the paper with your finger
Hold your finger in the sun
80067.e: With ink from an ink pad, the pattern of lines stays visible on the paper. That way you can compare prints.
80067.m: You can make fingerprints with an ink pad.

80068.q: What do your fingers leave behind when you touch a clean drinking glass?
80068.e: The skin gives off a little grease and sweat. That is why fingerprints are left behind on smooth surfaces such as glass.
80068.m: Fingerprints are left behind on glass.

80069.q: What is the soft, round end of a finger called?
80069.e: The fingertip is the soft pad at the front end of the finger. You use it to touch and feel.
80069.m: The end of the finger is called the fingertip.

80070.q: What do blind people use to read Braille?
80070.e: Braille is made of small raised dots. Blind people feel them with their fingertips.
80070.m: You read Braille with your fingertips.

80071.q: Which part of the hand can feel things most finely?
80071.e: There are particularly many nerves in the fingertips. That is why you can feel even tiny differences there.
80071.m: The fingertips feel things especially finely.

80072.q: What do your fingertips look like after a long bath?
80072.e: After a long time in water, the skin on the fingertips gets wrinkles. After drying off, it becomes smooth again.
80072.m: After a bath your fingertips are wrinkly.

80073.q: What do guitar players often get on their fingertips over time?
80073.e: When playing the guitar, the fingertips press hard on the strings. The skin protects itself by forming hard skin.
80073.m: Guitar players often have hard skin on their fingertips.

80074.q: Which part of the finger is best for using a phone screen?
80074.e: A touchscreen reacts to skin. With a hard fingernail it usually does not work.
80074.m: You use a touchscreen with your fingertip.

80075.q: What do you put on your finger when sewing so that the needle does not prick your fingertip?
80075.e: A thimble is a little cap made of metal or plastic. With it you push the needle through the fabric without pricking yourself.
80075.m: A thimble protects your fingertip when sewing.

80076.q: What is on the top of the finger, directly above the fingertip?
80076.e: Underneath, at the end of the finger, is the soft fingertip. Above it sits the hard fingernail, which protects it.
80076.m: The fingernail sits above the fingertip.

80077.e: Fingernails are made of horny cells containing the substance keratin. Hair is made of it too.

80078.q: Why does it not hurt to cut your fingernails?
a: The front of the nail has no nerves
The scissors only press very gently
The skin holds back the pain
80078.e: There are no nerves in the white front part of the nail. That is why you feel no pain when you cut it.
80078.m: The front part of the nail has no nerves.

80079.q: What is the pale curve at the bottom of the fingernail called?
80079.e: At the bottom of the nail you can often see a pale curve. It is called the lunula, which means ‘little moon’, because it looks like a half-moon.
80079.m: The pale curve at the bottom of the nail is called the lunula.

80080.q: Roughly how much does a fingernail grow in a month?
80080.e: Fingernails grow slowly, about half a millimetre to one millimetre a week. In a month that is only a few millimetres.
80080.m: Fingernails only grow a few millimetres a month.

80081.e: The hard nail protects the sensitive fingertip. It also helps you pick up small things.

80082.q: Which grow faster: fingernails or toenails?
80082.e: Fingernails grow faster than toenails. That is why you have to cut them more often.

80083.q: What is the thin skin at the bottom edge of the fingernail called?
80083.e: The cuticle is at the bottom edge of the nail. It protects the place where the nail grows from.
80083.m: The cuticle protects the root of the nail.

80084.q: What is best for cutting fingernails?
80084.e: Nail scissors are small and often have curved blades. With them you can trim your nails neatly.
80084.m: You cut fingernails with nail scissors.

80085.q: What do cats have on their paws where we have fingernails?
80085.e: Cats have sharp claws. They can stick them out and pull them back in.
80085.m: Cats have claws instead of flat nails.

80086.q: How many fingernails does a person usually have?
80086.e: A person has two hands with five fingers each. There is a nail on each finger, so that makes ten.

80087.q: What happens to a fingernail after you have cut it?
80087.e: The nail keeps growing from the nail root. That is why you have to keep cutting your nails.

80088.q: What helps you pick up a coin from a smooth table?
80088.e: With the hard edge of your fingernails you can get under the flat coin. With the soft fingertip alone it is difficult.
80088.m: Fingernails help you pick up small things.

80089.q: What is the outer side of the hand called?
80089.e: The top side of the hand is called the back of the hand. The inside is the palm.
80089.m: The outer side of the hand is called the back of the hand.

80090.q: What can you often see showing through the skin on the back of your hand in a bluish colour?
80090.e: On the back of the hand the skin is thin. That is why you can see the veins as bluish lines.
80090.m: You can often see the veins on the back of your hand.

80091.q: What do you see as little hills on the back of your hand when you make a fist?
80091.e: When you make a fist, your knuckles stick out. They are the joints between the hand and the fingers.
80091.m: When you make a fist, you can see your knuckles.

80092.q: Which side of the hand faces upwards when you lay your hand flat on the table?
80092.e: When you lay your hand flat, the palm lies on the table. On top you then see the back of the hand.
80092.m: When your hand lies flat, the back of the hand is on top.

80093.q: What moves under the skin on the back of your hand when you move your fingers?
80093.e: Tendons connect the muscles in the arm to the fingers. On the back of the hand you can see them as cords when you straighten your fingers.

80094.q: Where on the hand do doctors in hospital often put a needle for a drip?
a: On the back of the hand
80094.e: On the back of the hand, the veins are close under the skin. That is why it is a good place to put in a needle for a drip.
80094.m: Drips are often given through the back of the hand.

80095.q: Where on the hand do fine hairs grow for many people?
a: On the back of the hand
80095.e: There are hair roots on the back of the hand. That is why fine hairs grow there for many people.
80095.m: Fine hairs grow on the back of the hand.

80096.q: What do you call a person who mainly writes with their left hand?
80096.e: If you use your left hand more skilfully, you are a left-hander. Left-handers usually write, draw and throw with their left.
80096.m: If you write with your left hand, you are a left-hander.

80097.q: Roughly how many people are left-handed?
80097.e: It is estimated that about ten per cent of people are left-handed. That is about one person in ten.
80097.m: About one person in ten is left-handed.

80098.q: Which scissors are best for left-handers?
80098.e: On left-handed scissors the blades are arranged the other way round. That way a left-hander can see the line well while cutting.

80099.q: On which day is International Left-Handers Day?
80099.e: International Left-Handers Day is celebrated every year on 13 August. It draws attention to the needs of left-handers.

80100.q: What are left-handed children told today?
a: They may write with their left hand
They must write with their right hand
They may not write at all
They must write with their foot
80100.e: In the past, left-handers were often forced to write with their right hand. Today we know that they should write with their strong left hand.
80100.m: Left-handers may write with their left hand.

80101.q: What can easily happen to left-handers when they write with ink?
80101.e: We write from left to right. So the left hand moves over the fresh ink and can smudge it.
80101.m: Left-handers have to watch out for fresh ink.

80102.q: Can you choose whether you become left-handed?
a: No, you are usually born that way
Yes, you choose at the age of 10
Yes, it is drawn by lot
80102.e: Whether you are left-handed is usually something you are born with. You can already tell in small children.
80102.m: Left-handedness is usually something you are born with.

80103.q: What can you buy specially for left-handers to make writing easier?
80103.e: There are fountain pens with a special nib for left-handers. With them there is less scratching and fewer blots when writing.
80103.m: There are special fountain pens for left-handers.

80104.q: What do you call a person who can use both hands equally well?
80104.e: If you can use both hands equally skilfully, you are ambidextrous. That is quite rare.
80104.m: An ambidextrous person can use both hands equally well.

80105.q: Which half of the brain mainly controls the right hand?
80105.e: The brain controls the sides of the body crosswise. The left half of the brain steers the right side of the body.
80105.m: The left half of the brain controls the right hand.

80106.q: Which hand do people in Switzerland usually shake when greeting each other?
80106.e: When shaking hands in Switzerland, people give each other their right hand. This also applies to left-handers.
80106.m: When greeting, you give your right hand.

80107.q: On which side of the plate does the knife go when laying the table?
80107.e: The knife goes on the right of the plate and the fork on the left. That way it is comfortable for cutting for most people.
80107.m: The knife goes on the right of the plate.

80108.q: How can you often tell whether a small child is right-handed?
a: They mostly grab and draw with their right hand
They have more hair on the right
They sleep on their right side
They have bigger ears on the right
80108.e: Children show their strong hand when they grab, draw and throw. If a child mostly uses the right hand, they are probably right-handed.
80108.m: The hand a child draws with is usually their strong hand.

80109.q: On which side of the keyboard is the computer mouse usually placed for right-handers?
80109.e: Right-handers use the mouse with their right hand. That is why it lies to the right of the keyboard.
80109.m: Right-handers have the mouse on the right.

80110.q: Which hand is usually a little stronger in right-handers?
80110.e: Right-handers use their right hand more often. That is why it is usually a little stronger and more skilful.
80110.m: In right-handers, the right hand is often stronger.

80111.q: Which hand does a right-hander write with?
80111.e: A right-hander uses their right hand for fine work such as writing. It is their skilful hand.
80111.m: Right-handers write with their right hand.

80112.q: Which two fingers do you usually use to click your fingers?
80112.e: To click your fingers, you press your middle finger firmly against your thumb. Then it slips off and hits the base of your hand. That makes the sound.
80112.m: You usually click your fingers with your thumb and middle finger.

80113.q: Which part of the hand do many parents use to check quickly whether a child's forehead is hot?
80113.e: The skin on the back of the hand feels warmth well. That is why many parents put the back of their hand on the forehead when a child seems ill.
80113.m: The back of the hand feels warmth well.

a: A place where water comes out of the ground
A lake high up in the mountains
A place where a river ends
80310.e: At a spring, water comes out of the ground or out of a rock into the daylight. A stream often starts there.
80310.m: At a spring, water comes out of the earth.

80311.q: Why is spring water often cool even in summer?
a: It comes from the cool ground
It flows over blocks of ice
It falls from the sky at night
80311.e: Deep in the ground it stays about equally cool all year. That is why spring water is pleasantly fresh even on hot days.
80311.m: Spring water comes up cool from deep down.

80312.q: What is a spring called that warm water comes out of?
80312.e: The water of a thermal spring is heated deep inside the Earth. In Switzerland there are such springs in Baden or Leukerbad, for example.
80312.m: Warm water bubbles out of a thermal spring.

80313.q: What is a hot spring called that shoots water high into the air again and again?
